S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

info.persona: Nancy Pratt blends a love for routine with a contagious talkative flair, meticulously planning routes, garden beds, and dinner parties while occasionally allowing an overdue laundry pile to become a comedic saga that fuels their next volunteer event.
info.professional_persona: Nancy Pratt is a transportation operations specialist in Quincy, Massachusetts, leveraging her associate’s degree in transportation management and GIS mapping expertise; they methodically optimize routes, ensure DOT compliance, and communicate clearly with drivers and customers, all while channeling their sociable energy toward mentoring new staff and eyeing a supervisory role.
info.cultural_background: Nancy comes from a white New England background, with family roots in the Boston suburbs that stretch back several generations. Her upbringing in Quincy emphasized community involvement, reliability, and a practical approach to daily life, reflecting broader New England cultural values of punctuality, self-reliance, and modesty. Her family traditions include regular church attendance, civic volunteering, and multi-generation family gatherings that celebrate holidays with traditional American fare. This cultural environment has reinforced her preference for routine, her organized work style, and her sociable, community-oriented outlook.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Nancy enjoys activities that blend routine with social interaction. She regularly volunteers at her local community center, helping organize neighborhood events and leading a weekly senior-transportation assistance program. Her love of hospitality shines when she hosts dinner parties for family and friends, where she showcases her cooking and organized entertaining skills. She maintains a small vegetable garden, finds satisfaction in the predictable cycle of planting and harvesting, and cycles along the Quincy waterfront for fitness. Nancy is also a member of a church choir, enjoys knitting and crochet projects, and participates in a co-ed softball league, where her talkative nature makes her a natural team motivator. When she needs quiet time, she works on crossword puzzles and reads practical non-fiction on home organization.
info.sports_persona: Nancy Pratt energizes the Quincy Mariners co‑ed softball league as a vocal captain, cycles the Quincy waterfront three times a week for cardio, and follows the Boston Red Sox and Boston Celtics, often attending games when the schedule aligns with their routine.
info.arts_persona: Nancy Pratt sings in her local church choir performing hymns by Matt Maher, relaxes knitting scarves inspired by patterns from Ravelry, solves New York Times crossword puzzles, and regularly streams folk‑rock artist Gillian Welch while crocheting, weaving these creative pursuits into their structured evenings.
info.travel_persona: Nancy Pratt plans low‑cost weekend getaways with meticulously mapped itineraries, favoring New England coastal towns such as Rockport and Nantucket, the historic streets of Charleston, South Carolina, and dreaming of a week exploring the vineyards of Tuscany, all while balancing travel expenses against their savings goals and occasional family obligations.
info.culinary_persona: Nancy Pratt cultivates a small vegetable garden of homegrown tomatoes, heirloom carrots, and basil, then showcases these harvests in garden‑fresh ratatouille, herb‑crusted chicken, and a basil‑pesto pasta at dinner parties, where they also serve regional favorites like New England clam chowder, delighting guests with both flavor and meticulous table setting.

info.persona: Luis Cumplido, a disciplined yet low‑key competitor, blends solitary rigor with a quiet love for community rhythm, constantly measuring each choice against efficiency and personal fulfillment.
info.professional_persona: Luis Cumplido, an experienced emergency medical technician with ACLS and PHTLS certifications, uses their methodical, data‑driven mindset and bilingual fluency to excel in rapid triage while quietly challenging protocols to improve unit efficiency and mentor newer EMTs, all in pursuit of a future paramedic role and shift‑supervisor leadership.
info.cultural_background: Luis was raised in a Cuban‑American household in Miami’s Little Havana, where Spanish was spoken at home and Cuban traditions were celebrated. He grew up with the rhythms of son, salsa, and rumba, and family gatherings centered around shared meals and storytelling. This bicultural upbringing instilled a strong sense of resilience, community responsibility, and pride in his heritage. Though he identifies as an independent individual, Luis maintains close ties to the local Cuban community, participating in cultural festivals and supporting neighborhood initiatives that preserve Cuban art, music, and cuisine.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime, Luis enjoys solitary activities that provide both mental focus and physical release. He frequents the Atlantic coast for early‑morning fishing trips, finding the routine calming yet flexible. Running along South Beach’s promenade and weightlifting at a local gym help him maintain the stamina required for his demanding shifts. He also nurtures his cultural roots by playing the tres, a traditional Cuban guitar, and cooking classic dishes such as ropa vieja and yuca con mojo. A puzzle‑loving mind leads him to play chess and read science‑fiction novels, while he occasionally joins small groups of friends for a game of basketball.
info.sports_persona: Luis Cumplido, an avid runner who logs early‑morning miles along South Beach’s promenade, lifts at Miami Iron Gym, joins pickup basketball games with a close friend group, and roots for the Miami Heat and Miami Dolphins, embodies a disciplined yet casually competitive approach to fitness.
info.arts_persona: Luis Cumplido, a devoted tres player who winds down after shifts by improvising to the sounds of Buena Vista Social Club and Celia Cruz, pairs that with evenings of sci‑fi novels by Isaac Asimov and occasional viewings of Pedro Almodóvar’s films, letting music and narrative fuel their solitary creativity.
info.travel_persona: Luis Cumplido, a weekend explorer who prefers spontaneous, low‑key trips—fishing in the Florida Keys, weekend road‑tripping to Key West, and occasional island getaways to Bermuda—balances work‑shift constraints with a love for coastal breezes and cultural festivals.
info.culinary_persona: Luis Cumplido, an adept home cook who masters classics like ropa vieja, yuca con mojo, and crispy tostones, layers flavors with garlic, citrus, and fresh cilantro, and enjoys pairing their meals with catches from early‑morning fishing trips, yet admits to overindulging on fried snacks during late‑night cravings.

info.persona: Leona Joseph is a curiosity‑driven mental‑health advocate who balances a chaotic schedule with art, yoga, and a penchant for over‑spicing her cooking, all while wrestling with persistent anxiety and a love for spontaneous cultural adventures.
info.professional_persona: Leona Joseph is a seasoned mental‑health and substance‑abuse social worker in New York City who blends trauma‑informed counseling with art‑based interventions, leveraging her curiosity and collaborative yet assertive style to build trust and develop community‑driven programs, even though her relaxed approach to scheduling sometimes means she juggles multiple grant deadlines and case loads in a delightfully chaotic fashion.
info.cultural_background: Leona identifies as African‑American and grew up in a close‑knit Black community within the Bronx before moving to Manhattan for her graduate studies. Her upbringing was shaped by church gatherings, family storytelling, and a rich tradition of music and dance, all of which cultivated a deep appreciation for cultural expression. In her professional life, she draws on this heritage to provide culturally attuned care, incorporating Afrocentric perspectives, community strengths, and historical contexts into her therapeutic approach. Living in New York’s diverse boroughs, she remains connected to Black cultural institutions, neighborhood festivals, and activist networks that reinforce her commitment to social justice and empowerment for marginalized groups.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Leona’s curiosity drives her to explore New York’s vibrant arts scene; she spends weekends wandering galleries, attending spoken‑word poetry events, and sketching in Central Park. She enjoys reading contemporary fiction and African‑American literature, practicing yoga and mindfulness meditation to counterbalance her stress‑prone disposition, and cooking Afro‑Caribbean dishes that connect her to family traditions. She also volunteers at a community garden, participates in local jazz jam sessions, and maintains a personal journal where she reflects on her experiences and ideas for creative interventions.
info.sports_persona: Leona Joseph enjoys low‑impact fitness, attending sunrise yoga classes at the community center, joining a casual walking club that meets in Central Park on Saturdays, and cheering on the New York Knicks and Yankees, while occasionally dabbling in recreational pickleball at a local gym.
info.arts_persona: Leona Joseph immerses herself in New York’s creative pulse by sketching in Central Park, attending spoken‑word poetry nights featuring artists like Sarah Kay, exploring contemporary exhibitions at the Museum of Modern Art, and participating in late‑night jazz jam sessions at the Blue Note, where her love of narrative storytelling fuels both her personal art practice and her therapeutic work.
info.travel_persona: Leona Joseph prefers spontaneous weekend getaways that blend cultural immersion with culinary exploration, such as a recent visit to Kingston to sample authentic jerk cuisine, a planned trip to Lisbon to trace historic maritime routes, and local day trips to the Hudson Valley’s farm‑to‑table festivals, all balanced against her modest travel budget and family commitments.
info.culinary_persona: Leona Joseph delights in cooking vibrant Caribbean‑inspired dishes like spicy jerk chicken, creamy coconut rice, callaloo soup, and sweet plantain fritters, often experimenting with locally sourced herbs and fresh seafood while sharing meals with friends at her cozy Brooklyn apartment, though she sometimes over‑spices dishes in her enthusiasm for bold flavors.
